name: Pixel Art. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics. Provenance: explicit. The source explicitly requests pixel art and a 16-bit sprite appearance.
visualIdentity: Explicit: low logical resolution, limited palette, whole-pixel placement, and deliberate pixel clusters. Key poses are animated with few in-between frames. Palette cycling animates water, neon, or day-night changes without moving silhouette pixels. Scaling uses integer factors with smoothing disabled. A 320 x 180 canvas and a 32-color palette are optional examples, not requirements. The note states that suggested details were not verified in the source video.
suitableUses: Explicit: pixel art and 16-bit sprite-style visuals. Inferred from suggested combinations, not verified: chiptune videos, game trailers, looping social clips, and city-builder explainers or map overviews when paired with an isometric grid. Other uses, such as corporate or photographic topics, are unspecified and would need task-level judgment.
limitations: Avoid smoothing or non-integer scaling, which blurs pixel clusters. Do not use post-effects that blend palette indices. Thirty-two colors is not a universal 16-bit constraint. Palette cycling must remain discrete, with no interpolation or full-screen flashing swaps. Text legibility and pixel-font glyph support are unspecified and need checking. Simulated appearance does not establish physical production or validated physics.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: six discrete base colors. Roles are background #18253A, foreground #F3EBD3, accent_1 #426A76, accent_2 #8AA386, accent_3 #D3A45E, and accent_4 #B56D6F. Task-provided exact colors override these. Gradients are disabled. Two-color contrast: foreground on background is 12.923:1, and accent_1 with foreground is 4.961:1, both passing 4.5:1. Accent_2 with background (5.616:1) and accent_3 with background (6.773:1) also pass. Accent_4 at 3.944:1 is decorative only. Composited frames must be rechecked.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: poses hold with few in-between frames, and palette cycling stays discrete. Sprite placement stays on whole pixels, and delivery frame rate may exceed pose exposure rate. Interactive behavior for this style is unspecified. Optional motion references are not required. Motion-006 (bounded pupil-following gaze) needs eye layers or a rig and is not viewer eye tracking. Motion-012 (chaptered transition) and motion-015 (scroll storytelling) need compatible scene states. Each must be screened against the actual scene, and interactive delivery should freeze palette cycling under reduced motion.
audio: Audio is unspecified in the style data and is a task-level choice. Options include background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence, selected from topic, audience, and objective. Beat-table scheduling of poses and palette cycles is suggested only for chiptune-style combinations. Interactive audio must be user-started. No audio asset is supplied or mandated. Speech intelligibility, audio balance, and absence of clipping need verification in the final video.
assetRequirements: Specified: indexed sprites or pixel clusters drawn at integer coordinates on a fixed-resolution offscreen canvas. Palette indices must stay separate from colors, and selected indices may rotate over time. Aseprite, an optional supporting tool, can create sprites, palettes, and frame animations, and export sprite sheets or numbered PNGs. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Stateful simulations should be cached first. Exact source artwork and colors, if supplied, must be preserved.
combinations: Pixel Art can stand alone for sprites and scenes on a fixed logical grid. Suggested hybrid one pairs style-105 for beat-table timing of key poses and palette cycles, with whole-pixel positions and no live-analysis drift. Suggested hybrid two pairs style-077 for a 2:1 pixel isometric tile grid, with labels in a separate crisp text layer and the six-color palette. Avoid Three.js perspective, arbitrary-angle rotation, and anti-aliased edges. These combinations are suggestions, not verified outcomes.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default render pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a conditional fallback, used only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. An existing React project alone is not a reason. Canvas 2D is the primary style renderer, with PixiJS optional for large sprite sets and p5.js optional with nearest-neighbor enlargement. The motion engine owns movement, with one owner per property. Chroma.js validates palette contrast. Delivery checks cover opening, action, transition, and closing frames, plus dimensions, frame rate, audio sync, and loop continuity.
